mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS drops > 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over 3 months signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST) and increasing retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both increase.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals accommodative monetary policy with potential overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases > 2% QoQ.
